description: Merging: platformAutomerge, so the forge (GitHub auto-merge, GitLab merge when pipeline succeeds) merges an automerge PR the moment its required checks pass, any day, instead of waiting for Renovate's next visit. That is only safe where the branch rules require the real CI checks: every public GitHub repository's ruleset requires its CI jobs and the PR title check, and every GitLab project requires a green pipeline. A repository without that (a private one on GitHub Free, which gets no rulesets) or one with a merge window (platformAutomerge ignores automergeSchedule: the forge merges whenever the checks pass) sets platformAutomerge false.

rebaseWhen conflicted: auto rebased every automerge PR that fell behind the default branch, and each rebase cost a CI run. The rulesets do not require a branch to be up to date and the merges are squash or merge commits, so a branch behind main still merges.

prHourlyLimit 0 with prConcurrentLimit and branchConcurrentLimit 20: Renovate's default of 2 PRs an hour parked updates under Rate-Limited, or pushed them as PR-less branches, while the queue was half empty; the concurrent limits already bound open PRs.
prBodyNotes: {{#if isVulnerabilityAlert}}🔒 **Security fix**: it skips the age gate and the merge window.{{/if}}

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: CVE-triggered PRs (OSV/GitHub Advisory on a version you use): no age gate, no schedule. The prefix is fix(security): for anything that ships and chore(security): for a development-only dependency (npm devDependencies, composer require-dev, PEP 735 dependency-groups, uv and PDM dev-dependencies, Poetry dev-dependencies and its dev group): auto-release releases at once only on fix(security):, and a dev-only fix changes no image or package, so it waits for the next regular release. A template, not a package rule: this block is force, so a rule could never change what it sets. Renovate applies this block as force: it is spread over the result of every later merge, so whatever it sets replaces, never adds. It therefore sets nothing about merging or labelling: automerge here would also merge a major version, and labels, addLabels or prBodyNotes here would wipe the automerge/manual-review label, the major label and the manual rules' note. The security label and note come from the top-level addLabels and prBodyNotes templates instead, which are appended. 1-minute floor (not 0 days) ensures Renovate posts a stability check: 0 days normalises to null internally, no check is posted, and GitHub returns state: pending with empty statuses, which blocks automerge on repos without CI. timestamp-optional because CVE fix packages may lack a releaseTimestamp. commitMessageSuffix is emptied: Renovate's default [SECURITY] only repeated the fix(security): prefix and the security label.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly refresh of every lock file to the newest versions the ranges allow, transitive ones included. Renovate posts no stability check for it, but hands minimumReleaseAge to two package managers: npm install --before=<now minus 7 days> and Poetry's POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE, so npm and Poetry lock files take only releases at least 7 days old. uv.lock honours [tool.uv] exclude-newer (the uv consumers set 7 days). Those automerge (the lock file rule below); every other lock file takes whatever is newest: composer's refresh is off (php-ci audits the lock instead), and cargo, bundler and the rest wait for a person (the manual lock file rule at the end, which also makes them monthly). timestamp-optional because the update has no release timestamp, so with the default the branch would stay pending.

dockerhub-suffix.description: Docker Hub tags for images with more than 1,000 tags, where the docker datasource loses every release timestamp (see the packageRules that use it). One page, newest first, filtered to tags containing the pinned tag's suffix (3.12-alpine -> name=-alpine, 28-dind -> name=-dind), so the variants that matter are on it. Carries the per-tag digest: Renovate takes newDigest from the release, so tag@digest pins keep working, including same-tag digest updates. packageName is the Docker Hub repository (library/python).

lscr-linuxserver.description: linuxserver.io images (lscr.io/linuxserver/<image>), from their GitHub releases (linuxserver/docker-<image>): one release per published -lsN image tag, with its date; develop and nightly builds are prereleases and are dropped. Every build gets the earliest date among the builds of its upstream version (the tag minus -lsN; a build suffix such as _v<library> stays in the key, so a library change waits its own gate): a new upstream version waits out the full age gate from its first build, later rebuilds of an aged version pass at once. sourceUrl points Renovate at the same repository, so the PR body carries each build's release notes. The newest 100 releases reach back months; one page of Docker Hub tags covered about 9 days for a busy image, so its 14 and 30-day gates could never pass and first builds were dated weeks late. packageName is the bare image name; a repository adds the regex manager that finds its pins and the versioning its tags need.

customManagers.description: Hugo version in workflow files (a hugo_version: value, or the default: under a hugo_version input of a reusable workflow or composite action). The hugo-version: input of peaceiris/actions-hugo is already handled by the built-in github-actions manager with the same depName, so every Hugo pin lands in one PR.

OpenTofu version passed to the reusable terraform-ci workflow (opentofu_version: input in callers, default: under the opentofu_version input here). Without it the pins went stale unseen (k3s-oci and the default sat at 1.9.1 while 1.13 was current). The depName joins the existing opentofu group, so every OpenTofu pin moves in one PR.

Python version passed to the reusable python-ci workflow (python_version: input in callers, default: under the python_version input here). Looked up like setup-python's own python-version input (actions/python-versions releases), so it joins the python group with the Dockerfile's base image and CI tests the version that ships. npm versioning keeps a two-part value two-part (3.14 to 3.15).

PHP version passed to the reusable php-ci workflow (php_version: input in callers, default: under the php_version input here), from php-src's php-X.Y.Z tags. Joins the php group with the Dockerfile's base image. npm versioning keeps a two-part value two-part (8.4 to 8.5).

pip-audit version the reusable python-ci workflow runs with uvx (pip_audit_version: input in callers, default: under the pip_audit_version input here), from PyPI. No built-in manager reads a workflow input.

OpenTofu version files (.opentofu-version, read by tenv from the nearest parent directory). The depName joins the opentofu group, so the local version and the CI pins move in one PR and cannot drift apart.

GitHub release assets a kustomization pulls as remote resources (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<file>, such as system-upgrade-controller's crd.yaml and manifest). depName is the owner/repo in the URL, so every URL of one release moves in the same PR. The kustomize manager reads images and Helm charts only.

packageRules.description: Major updates: hold 30 days to let the ecosystem surface breaking changes and incompatibilities. Whether they merge themselves is decided at the end: the low-risk majors rule automerges a few kinds, the manual major rule holds every other one for a person.
Patch and pin updates: hold 7 days to let the community catch supply-chain attacks before auto-merging on green CI

Digest and pinDigest updates: 1-minute floor forces Renovate to post a stability check. 0 days normalises to null internally (no check posted = branch stays pending forever on repos without CI). timestamp-optional required because a digest update's branch carries no releaseTimestamp (the lookup-level gate ages it against its tag's latest release where the datasource gives dates, but that date never reaches the branch) — with the default 'require' behaviour the branch stability check would stay PENDING forever regardless of how many times Renovate runs. Every consumer runs at least one real check (its CI, or the pr-title workflow), so internalChecksAsSuccess is off: automerge waits for those checks.

Third-party image digests (base-image rebuilds): Renovate ages a digest update against its tag's latest push (lookup applyMinimumReleaseAgeToDigestUpdate), so a short gate works where the registry gives dates (Docker Hub via the docker datasource, custom.dockerhub-suffix); ghcr/quay digests have no date and still pass (timestamp-optional). 2 days stays below the weekly-or-slower rebuild cadence of official images. pinDigest stays at the 1-minute floor: pinning the digest already in use brings in nothing new.
Minor updates: hold 14 days to let the community catch supply-chain attacks before auto-merging on green CI
Regex-managed versions: one PR per package; include from/to versions and update type
Regex-managed digest updates: no extra info in commit message — digest is self-explanatory
Regex-managed helm charts: add helm/ prefix, overrides topic from both version and digest regex rules above — commitMessageExtra is inherited from whichever of those matched first
Regex-managed container images: docker/ prefix and the bare image name, the same as images the kubernetes and dockerfile managers find.
kubernetes images: docker/ prefix, strip org/registry path keeping only image name, include from/to versions and update type
argocd: helm/ prefix, strip org/registry path keeping only chart name, include from/to versions and update type
helmfile/helm-values: helm/ prefix, strip org/registry keeping only chart name, include from/to versions and update type
kustomize: helm/ prefix for helmCharts, docker/ for images, org and registry stripped, both versions and the update type, the same as the other managers.

terraform: move only the lock file for in-range updates and leave the constraint alone (out-of-range majors still rewrite it). With bump, the constraint PR set the lock to its own age-gated newVersion and downgraded providers that lock file maintenance had already moved further (k3s-oci #186, oci 9.9.0 -> 9.8.0). An in-range lock update keeps its patch or minor update type (isLockfileUpdate is only a flag), so the age gates of those rules apply to it; lock file maintenance, which ages no provider, is off for terraform (see the terraform manager block). npm, composer and cargo need no such rule: the default rangeStrategy auto already resolves to update-lockfile for them and keeps their widen cases (peer dependencies, || ranges). The preset used to force bump on them, and bump takes its update candidates from the lowest version the range allows instead of the locked one, so it automerged downgrades below the lock (sunrise-sunset-calendar #129 and #140, phpstan 2.3.1 -> 2.3.0; thelounge-plugin-apprise-push #63, eslint 10.12.0 -> 10.11.0; thelounge-theme-chat #72, stylelint) and opened no-op 'from X to X' PRs. Kept in its own rule because Renovate rejects rangeStrategy together with matchUpdateTypes (the range strategy is decided before the update type is known).
terraform: terraform/ prefix, use resolved versions not constraint strings, include update type; currentVersion is absent for lockfile-only updates so make the 'from' clause conditional
dockerfile and GitLab CI job images: docker/ prefix, strip org/registry path keeping only image name, include from/to versions and update type
npm: add npm/ prefix, use resolved versions not constraint strings, include update type; dedupe lock file after each update

npm engines (package.json engines.node) in the TheLounge packages: a compatibility floor, not a dependency. Renovate raised thelounge-plugin-apprise-push's engines.node from >=18.20.8 to >=24.21.0 (#67) when no code needed it, and `thelounge install` refuses a package whose engines its Node (22) doesn't meet, so no release from 1.3.0 on could be installed. Scoped to these repositories: they are installed into TheLounge's own image, whose Node they can't choose. A person raises the floor when the code needs a newer runtime.
composer: composer/ prefix, from/to resolved versions and update type
github-actions: action/ prefix, strip org keeping only action name, include from/to versions and update type
GitHub-hosted runner images (runs-on: ubuntu-24.04) come through the github-actions manager but are not actions: runner/ prefix.

Version inputs of actions (tflint_version, node-version, ...) are plain versions extracted as depType uses-with; pinning them to a commit SHA cannot be written (Errored branch on Dependency Dashboard #4).

GitLab CI includes and components (include: project: ... ref: v1.0.0, component: ...@1.0.0) are looked up as gitlab-tags; pinning them to a commit SHA cannot be written ("Digest is not updated", then "Error updating branch: update failure" on renovate/pin-dependencies in every GitLab project, 2026-10-23).
GitLab CI includes and components (the mbologna/ci-templates include): ci/ prefix and both versions, like the other managers' titles.

mbologna/.github reusable workflows: already age-gated by that repo's own Renovate run, so no stability window; automerge on green CI, no reviewer. 1-minute floor (not 0 days) ensures Renovate posts a stability check on every branch. timestamp-optional because github-digest SHAs carry no releaseTimestamp. commitMessageExtra includes newDigestShort so each PR title is unique (without it Renovate disables automerge on later PRs with the same title). MUST be placed after the github-actions digest rule so its commitMessageExtra wins. Weekly (Monday or Tuesday), and updateNotScheduled false: .github gets commits most days, and Renovate otherwise rebased every consumer's open pin PR after each of them, which was half of all builds on Renovate branches; now the branch moves only on the schedule days. An urgent workflow fix needs a manual merge in the repos that need it.

GitHub Actions digest updates (a moved major tag such as actions/checkout v7) wait 7 days like a patch, aged against the newest release that tag matches (v7.0.2 when v7 moves to it). A branch ref (master) has no release and stays ungated. Every action is SHA-pinned, so the age gate is what stands between a moved tag and every repository. Not the reusable workflows from mbologna/.github, which are reviewed where they change.

One weekly PR per repository for all GitHub Actions updates (majors still separate), opened on Monday or Tuesday and merged once CI passes: patch, minor and digest updates of every publisher automerge after their age gate (patch 7 days, minor 14, digest 7), because every action is SHA-pinned and the gate gives others time to notice a hijacked release. Majors are decided at the end (trusted publishers' majors automerge after 30 days; every other publisher's wait for a person). Not mbologna/.github's own reusable workflows, which have their own weekly rule, and not the runtime version inputs (setup-python's python-version and friends), which join their language's group.

pip_requirements/pip-compile: pip/ prefix, use constraint strings (deps may be unpinned), include update type. A lock-file-only update of an indirect dependency (a security fix in a pip-compile lock) has no currentValue or newValue, so it is titled with newVersion alone (the title used to read "update pip/certifi from to").

pip-compile lock refresh: the preset's lock file wording (maintain lock files). Renovate's pip-compile manager defaults the action to 'Refresh pip-compile outputs', whose capital fails a commitlint subject-case check. A package rule, because the manager's own default applies after the top-level lockFileMaintenance block.
pep621/poetry (pyproject.toml; pep621 also updates uv.lock, uv is not a Renovate manager): pip/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type

pre-commit hooks: hook/ prefix, strip org keeping only hook name, include from/to versions and update type; use currentValue/newValue (raw tag) since some repos use non-semver tags where currentVersion would be empty
bundler: gem/ prefix, from/to resolved versions and update type
docker-compose: docker/ prefix, strip org/registry keeping only image name, include from/to versions and update type
cargo: rust/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type

gomod: go/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type. gomodTidy: without it Renovate only edits go.mod and adds the new sums, leaving the old versions' sums in go.sum, so go-ci's go mod tidy -diff failed every Go update (agent-history-viewer#12, 2026-10-30). gomodUpdateImportPaths rewrites imports on a /vN major; a major that changes the module's domain (github.com/charmbracelet to charm.land) still needs a person.
maven: maven/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type
gradle/gradle-wrapper: gradle/ prefix, use resolved versions, include update type
nvm/.nvmrc/.node-version: node/ prefix, include from/to versions and update type

Every digest update, in one place: the tag that moved, the old and new short digests and the update type, e.g. 'docker/debian stable-slim from 5f2c1a3 to a717a33 (digest)'. Placed after the per-manager rules (which also match digest updates, for their topic) so it overrides their version-style extra. The short digest also keeps titles unique: Renovate treats two pull requests with the same title as the same update, and would switch automerge off for every digest bump after the first.
github-actions pin/pinDigest: lowercase action word, show target SHA, include update type (built-in uses capital Pin and overrides topic)

renovate/renovate image: prefix PR title with docker/. Changelog disabled — Renovate releases many times per day; fetching 10+ release notes from GitHub API hangs the runner. Its release dates come from GitHub releases, see the Docker Hub lookup rules below.

Docker Hub images with >1,000 tags, part 1. Docker Hub's tags API returns 403 past page 10; Renovate then drops the Docker Hub data for the whole image and falls back to the registry tag list, which has no timestamps, so every update sat in Pending Status Checks forever (2026-10-13). timestamp-optional would turn the age gate off, so look the versions up where the dates are. Keep these rules after every rule that matches matchDatasources docker (repo-level rules come after the preset's, so a repo rule matching docker would not see these images). renovate/renovate: GitHub releases have the same versions (tags without a v) with dates. Not npm, Renovate's documented overrideDatasource example: npm releases carry their integrity hash as newDigest, and the kubernetes manager writes any newDigest into the image, whatever pinDigests says, so 06898c5d pinned renovate/renovate:44.132.2@sha512-…, which no registry can pull (renovate-20261016-131513.log).

Docker Hub images with >1,000 tags, part 2 (fixed version tags): GitHub releases have the same versions with dates and full history. Docker Hub's newest 100 tags are nightlies for these, so the dockerhub-suffix datasource would miss stable releases. None of these is digest-pinned (github-releases digests are commit SHAs, not image digests).

Docker Hub images with >1,000 tags, part 3 (suffixed or floating tags, some tag@digest pinned; python, nginx, docker, nginx-unprivileged, node, catthehacker/ubuntu): the custom dockerhub-suffix datasource. Their release date is the tag's last push, so a floating tag such as 3.15-alpine ages from its latest rebuild, the same as any smaller Docker Hub image. The Hub API wants namespace/name: strip docker.io/ and prefix official images with library/.

Date-less registries, part 1: ghcr.io, nvcr.io and data.forgejo.org give the docker datasource no release timestamps, so updates sat in Pending Status Checks forever (2026-10-13). ghcr.io images come from the GitHub repo of the same owner/name and are tagged like its releases; a future one whose repo differs fails its lookup loudly. Only two-level ghcr paths: deeper ones are OCI Helm charts with no such repo. Excluded: mbologna's images, digest-only pins, and every tag@sha256 pin (matchJsonata, in parts 1-5): after an override the digest comes from the new datasource, a git commit SHA, which Renovate wrote into ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.24@5411378... and broke the builds (2026-10-21); see the digest-pinned rule below. This part: vX.Y.Z pins.
Date-less registries, part 2: ghcr.io pins tagged X.Y.Z, from GitHub releases tagged vX.Y.Z or X.Y.Z (the v is optional: astral-sh/uv tags 0.12.24, and a required v dropped every uv release).
Date-less registries, part 3: nvcr.io k8s-device-plugin from its GitHub releases (same vX.Y.Z tags).
Date-less registries, part 4: the Forgejo runner image (data.forgejo.org) from its releases on code.forgejo.org, tagged vX.Y.Z for image X.Y.Z.

Date-less registries, part 5: codeberg.org images from their Forgejo releases (vX.Y.Z tag for image X.Y.Z); the codeberg registry gives the docker datasource no dates. Chart tags such as k8s-gateway-4.0.1 do not match extractVersion.

jq tags its GitHub releases jq-X.Y.Z. The date-less registries rule above sends a ghcr.io/jqlang/jq X.Y.Z pin to github-releases with extractVersion ^v?, so no release parsed ('Found no results from datasource that look like a version') and the pin went untracked. Matched by depName because the datasource has already changed.

The GitLab Runner image comes from registry.gitlab.com, which serves no release dates, so the age gate would hold every update; GitLab's own releases of gitlab-org/gitlab-runner carry the same vX.Y.Z versions, dated. Not Docker Hub's gitlab/gitlab-runner, which has over 15,000 tags.

Floating tags on custom.dockerhub-suffix (3.12-alpine, 1.29-alpine, 28-dind, and bare ones such as docker 28 or python 3.12): Docker Hub's date for them is the latest rebuild, and official images rebuild every week or two, so the 14-day minor and 30-day major gates could never pass (python 3.15, docker 29-dind, nginx-unprivileged 1.31, 2026-10-13). A short gate still bounds the real age: a tag 3 days past its latest rebuild is at least 3 days old. Fixed tags (1.31.6-alpine) keep the normal gates. Bare floating tags were left out until 2026-10-23, so docker:28 never got its 29 update: 29 is rebuilt more often than every 30 days, and 28, end-of-life and off the newest-100 page, could not even get a digest pin. Must stay after the dockerhub-suffix override rules, which change the datasource it matches.

Docker versioning for node images (node:<version>-<variant>), overriding config:recommended's workarounds:nodeDockerVersioning, which sets node versioning with a versionCompatibility that strips the variant (-trixie, -alpine) off the releases. The custom.dockerhub-suffix datasource above keys each digest by the full tag, so a digest update for 24.22.1-trixie found no release and failed with 'Could not determine new digest'. Docker versioning keeps the variant as the compatibility suffix. It also treats every Node major as stable, odd ones included; a major is a manual-review update anyway.

Any image published under mbologna/ (any registry, any depth, including future ones): an own build, not an external release, so no stability wait (1 minute, not 0 days: 0 days normalises to null, no stability status is posted and automerge blocks forever). timestamp-optional because registry.gitlab.com and ghcr.io have no tag timestamps, so the gate could never be met (2026-10-12).

kustomize release tags are kustomize/vX.Y.Z (the repo also tags api/, cmd/config/, kyaml/ modules). Without extractVersion no tag parses as a version and a kustomize version pinned from github-releases never gets an update.

Non-major PyPI and npm updates: one PR a week per repository, opened on Monday or Tuesday. Each was its own PR and its own CI run (on GitLab, on the self-hosted runner, two jobs at a time). Placed before the preset's other groups, so the uv, python, dev tooling and Docker base images groups still win for their members. Majors keep their own PR; security fixes are separate branches and never grouped.
One PR for every OpenTofu pin: CI install steps and .opentofu-version files

Python in one PR per repository: the Dockerfile's base image, the GitLab CI test image, the reusable workflows' python_version input and setup-python's python-version. They are the same language version, and separate PRs left CI testing 3.14 while the images ran 3.15 (5 repositories, 2026-11). Digest updates stay in the Docker base images group. A minor (3.15 to 3.16) is a new language version that removes deprecated APIs; it automerges like any minor because CI's version moves in the same PR, so green CI means the new version passed the tests.
PHP in one PR per repository, for the same reason as the Python group: the Dockerfile's base image and the reusable php-ci workflow's php_version input.

Hugo: one PR for all pins (workflow inputs, reusable workflow defaults, actions-hugo). Patches and minors automerge after their age gate: the caller's hugo-pr-build workflow builds the site with the new version, deploys a preview and checks it before merge, which catches what a release could break (a minor's template or default changes included). MUST come after the regex and github-actions rules above so its title wins.

uv: one PR per uv release for every place a repository pins it: uv from PyPI in requirements-uv.txt (hash-pinned, installed with pip in a Dockerfile's build stage), the uv image where a Dockerfile still copies it (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv, looked up on GitHub releases as astral-sh/uv), the uv_build backend in pyproject.toml and the setup-uv version input. One PR a week, opened on Monday or Tuesday: the PyPI members would get that schedule from the non-major dependencies group anyway, and the setup-uv input from the github-actions group, so the whole group shares it. They are the same release, and separate PRs left a repository's image and build backend on different uv versions between merges. Dockerfiles take uv from PyPI because PyPI gives the release date the digest-pinned ghcr.io image lacks: that image's updates could not be age-gated and waited for a person in every repository (the date-less digest-pinned rule), while the PyPI uv waits out the usual age gate and automerges; the pip_requirements manager refreshes the hashes. After the ghcr.io override rules, which must not lose the image's lookup.

Third-party base-image digests (Dockerfile, compose and GitLab CI job image rebuilds of php, python, buildpack-deps, leap, docker/dockerfile, ...): one PR per rebuild wave instead of one per image. Not weekly: a rebuild often carries OS security fixes, and its merge is the push on which auto-release's security strategy compares the old and new base images with Trivy and releases at once when fixable HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs are gone, so holding it would delay CVE fixes by up to a week. A merge builds nothing by itself: images are built when a release ships. Own images (mbologna/) are left out: they are own builds, not upstream rebuilds.

Dev tooling (npm devDependencies, composer require-dev: linters, formatters, test and release tools): one PR a week per repository, opened on Monday or Tuesday. They ship nothing to users and were about 27 separate PRs in two months. Patch and minor only: a major keeps its own PR. Monday or Tuesday rather than Monday morning: the hosted GitHub app visits a quiet repository irregularly and missed a 9-hour Monday window for weeks (mail2apprise, 2026-11).

Terraform providers: one PR a week per repository, opened on Monday or Tuesday. A merge deploys nothing (tofu apply is a separate step), and each provider had its own PR. Patch and minor only: a major keeps its own PR, where the repository asks for a plan before merging.

pre-commit hook version bumps: one PR a week per repository, opened on Monday or Tuesday, like the other tooling groups. They only change local and CI checks. Digest updates keep their own manual rule (a moved tag).

Helm chart patch and minor updates: one PR a week per repository, opened on Monday or Tuesday, instead of a chain of PRs as a chart moves 10.9.7, 10.10.3, 10.10.5 in a week. A repository whose image scanner expedites single chart PRs sets groupName null for helm and keeps the weekly schedule.

Lock file maintenance automerges where the package manager holds the refresh to releases at least 7 days old: npm (install --before), Poetry (POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE), uv.lock under pep621, whose consumers all set [tool.uv] exclude-newer = "7 days", and pip-compile, whose lock Renovate regenerates with the command in its header, so a repository that enables the pip-compile manager compiles with uv pip compile --exclude-newer P7D. A repository whose lock lacks that setting must add it before relying on this rule. Composer, cargo, bundler and the rest take whatever is newest, so they keep the manual review at the end.

mbologna/ci-templates GitLab CI components: my own code, reviewed and age-gated in that project, so like mbologna/.github they skip the stability window, majors included, and automerge in one weekly MR per project. The 1-minute floor and timestamp-optional for the same reasons as the .github rule.

Low-risk majors automerge after the 30-day hold, on green CI: the trusted publishers' GitHub Actions (actions/*, github/*, docker/*, astral-sh/*, google-github-actions/*, sigstore/*, peaceiris/*; their majors are almost always a new Node runtime for the action), GitHub-hosted runner images (ubuntu-24.04 to 26.04) and my own packages (anything under mbologna/, whose majors I wrote). Runtime version inputs (depType uses-with) are excluded: they are language versions. Must come right before the manual major rule, which excludes the same set.
matchJsonata: $contains($string(packageName), 'mbologna/') or datasource = 'github-runners' or (manager = 'github-actions' and depType != 'uses-with' and $contains($string(packageName), /^(actions|github|docker|astral-sh|google-github-actions|sigstore|peaceiris)\//))

packageRules.description: Every other major waits for a person after its 30-day hold. The manual rules come last and nothing after them turns automerge back on, so the label and the PR note always agree with what happens (prBodyNotes and addLabels are appended across matching rules and cannot be taken back by a later one). groupName null: a manual major gets its own PR, so it can never share a branch with updates that automerge (a group automerges only when every member may, and carries the union of their labels, which is how ci-templates MRs once showed both automerge and manual-review). Repository rules come later, so a lock-step group in a repository keeps its majors together.
matchJsonata: $not($contains($string(packageName), 'mbologna/') or datasource = 'github-runners' or (manager = 'github-actions' and depType != 'uses-with' and $contains($string(packageName), /^(actions|github|docker|astral-sh|google-github-actions|sigstore|peaceiris)\//)))
prBodyNotes: **Why this waits for you:** a major update, which may break things. It waited 30 days for others to report problems; read the release notes before merging.

packageRules.description: A pre-commit digest update means a release tag now points at a different commit, the signature of a hijacked tag (tj-actions/changed-files). Hooks run in CI and on the laptop, so it never merges; and since the pinned commit is still the one that was reviewed, no PR is opened either: the repository stays on it, and the hook's next real release arrives as a normal, age-gated update.

Date-less registries, digest-pinned: ghcr.io tag@sha256 pins stay on the docker datasource (parts 1-5 skip them), which resolves real image digests but gives no release dates. A version bump therefore cannot be age-gated: it opens a PR for a person to review instead of sitting in Pending Status Checks unseen. Same-tag digest updates keep the digest rules.
prBodyNotes: **Why this waits for you:** the registry gives no release dates, so no age gate could apply. Read the upstream release notes before merging.

packageRules.description: Lock file maintenance for package managers that cannot hold a refresh to releases at least 7 days old (cargo, bundler, ...): a person merges it, once a month (days 1-3, so the GitHub app gets more than one chance to open it). composer is off altogether (the composer manager block): php-ci runs composer audit instead, so a vulnerable transitive package turns CI red rather than an ungated refresh merging. npm, Poetry, pep621 (uv.lock) and pip-compile locks are gated and automerge (the lock file rule above, and repository rules).
prBodyNotes: **Why this waits for you:** this package manager cannot hold a lock refresh to releases at least 7 days old, so it may bring in a release published today.

packageRules.description: Dependencies pinned to a branch's commit (the git-refs datasource: a '# renovate:' comment names the branch, and the new HEAD comes as a digest update). A commit has no release date, so no age gate can hold it, and it would automerge as soon as CI passed. A person reviews each one. A repository can group them and give them a weekly schedule.
prBodyNotes: **Why this waits for you:** a new commit on a branch the repository follows. It has no release, no release date and no age gate; read the upstream commits before merging.
